limitations: Linear models only (no constant term, no non-abelian or non-field structures); they give spectrum members, never gaps.
novelty_basis: Linear models over finite fields are a standard tool of the Equational Theories Project; the specific orders were not compared with the project's data. The membership 670 at n = 9 is not stated in Le Floch's notes (read for C05).
proof_check: computer-assisted - exhaustive search over GF(q)^2 for every prime power q <= 128 (EXP-C05-07; GF(q) is unique up to isomorphism, so the absence of a linear model does not depend on the representation); every model found re-checked on its full table with the generic evaluator; three tables Lean-certified by kernel decide (E677_order16_law, E1313_order16_law, E670_order9_law)
statement: For each of the 15 open ETP laws of EXP-C05-03 the prime powers q <= 128 admitting a linear model x*y = ax + by over GF(q) are exactly those listed in results/EXP-C05-07.json. In particular laws 670, 677, 1076, 1286 and 1313 have models of order 16 (1286 also of order 32), law 670 has a model of order 9, and no law has a linear model at an order excluded by the SAT search, the DRUP certificates (CLM-C05-08) or the ETP notes.
title: Linear models over finite fields: the orders q <= 128 at which the 15 open laws have a model x*y = ax + by over GF(q)
